::: {#rem-direct-proof-template}
#### The shape of a direct proof

A direct proof (@def-direct-proof) of "if $P$, then $Q$" has this shape:

> | Suppose $P$.
> | $\vdots$
> | Therefore $Q$.

Write the first and last lines first,
then fill in the middle,
usually by replacing each defined term with its definition (@rem-definitions-iff).

A direct proof proves $P \Rightarrow Q$:
when $P$ is true, the proof shows that $Q$ is true,
and when $P$ is false, $P \Rightarrow Q$ is true anyway (@def-implies).

When the statement is about every element of a set,
as in "for every odd integer $n$" (@def-universal-quantifier),
the proof starts from an arbitrary element:
"Suppose $n$ is an odd integer."
Since the proof uses nothing about $n$ except that $n$ is odd,
the same steps work for every odd integer.

:::
